lines.meet: I'm Fiona, a witch hunter. I'll stand in front, and I'll question everything anybody tells us, including you, so don't take it personally.
lines.meet_neighbour: Booty Bay, aye? I've seen you on the stairs. I'm Fiona, the one with the room full of files.
lines.ask_home: So, where's home? I'll check it against my notes, mind.
lines.ask_work: What was your line of work? I'd like the true version, not the one you tell at parties.
lines.answer_home: Aberdeen, the oil city, born and raised, then nine years in Dublin. Grey granite and a wind off the sea that goes straight through you.
lines.answer_work: Fraud, nine years, for an energy company. Padded invoices, ghost contractors and cooked safety records, mostly on rigs.
lines.chat_food: A strong cup of tea, so dark you could stand a spoon in it, and a buttery from the baker's in Aberdeen. Nothing else is worth discussing.
lines.chat_sleep: I sleep with my files under the bed. Nobody's touching those while I'm asleep, and nobody's touching them while I'm awake, either.
lines.chat_missing: The North Sea, if you can believe it. Grey and cold and miserable, and I'd stand on the beach at Aberdeen in a gale and be happy.
lines.chat_here: My first year here was a filing exercise. I catalogued every corrupted thing I met, and the notebook's more use now than I'll ever be.
lines.tease_quiet: {name}, you're harder to get a statement out of than a rig foreman. I respect it, professionally.
lines.tease_talker: As a witness, {name}, you'd be a disaster. You'd tell the whole story, then three more, and none of them under oath.
lines.tease_careful: {name}, you check everything twice before you sign it. Och, I could've used you in Dublin.
lines.tease_bold: {name}, you'd sign the form without reading it. I've investigated people like you, and they all said they were sure.
lines.tease_any: {name}, I've opened a file on you. It's mostly complaints, but there's a wee bit of praise at the bottom.
lines.tease_back: Aye, very good, {name}. I'll be adding that to your file.
lines.take_it_kindly: That's fair, I'll give you that one, {name}. Don't let it go to your head.
lines.bristle: Dinnae joke about that, {name}. I'm serious about it.
lines.apologise: That was out of line, and I'm sorry. I'm told I'm a lot, sometimes, and they're not wrong.
lines.double_down: I'm not retracting it. I've got evidence, and you know I have.
lines.needle_quiet: You saw something and you didn't report it. That's how a small problem becomes a big one.
lines.needle_talker: You talk and talk and none of it's evidence. Say the useful thing and stop.
lines.needle_careful: You've checked it three times, and you're still not sure. At some point you have to act on what you've got.
lines.needle_bold: You act without evidence, every time. I've written that down, and I'll keep writing it down.
lines.needle_any: You never check, and you never think to. I'm the one who has to clean up after.
lines.bite_back: I've checked everything you've done this week, and that's how I know I'm right. Look at your own file.
lines.hurt: Och, fine, point taken. I'll go and sort my notes for a while.
lines.laugh_off: Half a rig crew hated me for a month once. You'll have to do a lot better than that.
lines.confide: {name}, in my second year I worked out I'd been treating this war like a casework backlog, ticking things off. People aren't entries. That one landed hard.
lines.listen: I'll keep that off the record, {name}. Nobody's getting it out of me.
lines.look_out: {name}, keep behind me on this one. I've read the reports on what's in there, and I don't like them.
lines.accept: Fine, {name}, I'll go along with it. Noted, under protest.
lines.deflect: Och, wheesht, {name}, I'm fine. It's a wee scratch.
lines.check_in: Full report, {name}, not the short version. Where are you hurt?
lines.blame: Somebody went in without checking, and I've got a fair idea who. I'd put money on it.
lines.thank: You pulled me out of that one, and I'll not forget it. Thank you.
lines.brush_off: Aye, well, it needed doing. Sit down and get your breath back.
lines.worry: That was too close, {name}, and I don't like it. Sit still a minute.
lines.handed_down: If my records are right, and they usually are, this was yours. I'll keep it in good order.
lines.hand_fine: You can have it, that's fine. I travel with enough paper as it is.
lines.hand_sulk: I'd have signed off on it if anyone had bothered to ask me.
lines.turn_friendly: {name}, I trust your work. You check things, and that's rare.
lines.turn_friends: {name}, I'd show you my files. All of them. I've never said that to anybody.
lines.turn_grating: You and me aren't going to get on. I'd rather say it now than file it later.
lines.turn_rivals: I'll stand in front of you because the job needs it. That's the end of the report.
lines.make_up: I was wrong about you, {name}, and I'll put it in writing. Let's start again.
lines.defend: That's not what happened, and I was watching. Leave {name} out of it.
lines.friend_left: {name}'s off home for a while, and I've nobody to argue with properly.
lines.friend_back: About time, {name}! I've got three things I want to argue with you about.
lines.common_numbers: I spent nine years finding the one number that didn't fit. You've worked with figures too, haven't you? You check the totals.
lines.common_scots: You're Scottish too? Och, thank God. Where are you from, then?
